text:
Maya: Quick sync — I'm proposing a multi-dimension automatic fallback for canary rollouts: prefer model-variant fallback first, then regional failover, then capacity-based throttling. Want to avoid stomping session stickiness and KV-cache warmups. Thoughts?

Alex: +1 on variant-first. If we switch region too early we blow up cross-region limits and increase latency. Can we prefer a lightweight variant (quantized) with identical response shape? :thinking:

Sai: We need clear telemetry signals. I'm thinking: 1) rising 5m error-rate > 3% AND 95th latency increase > 2x triggers variant fallback; 2) if variant fallback fails OR instance-level OOMs spike, trigger regional failover. Also account for request affinity so chat sessions hit same model family.

Julie: UX question — how do we expose this in Console? Product wants a simple toggle + advanced policy JSON. Proposal: default (safe) = auto-fallback enabled with conservative thresholds; advanced = JSON editor for teams that want tight control. Also show expected cost delta in the rollout preview.

Maya: Good. Two tricky edge cases: 1) KV cache cold-start when you fallback to a different quantization (cache format mismatch) — prefer a warmup ramp (small % traffic) before full swap. 2) quota/backpressure: falling back to higher-capacity infra might hit org quota or per-region limits, so fallback should check soft-quota and attempt throttled ramp instead of full migration.

Alex: +1 on ramp. Suggestion for tie-breaker: if both variant and region eligible, prefer variant unless the variant's estimated tokens/sec < 50% of requested throughput. If it's too slow, pick regional failover.

Sai: Telemetry mapping details: keep a per-route signal composed of: token_latency_p50/p95, generation_errors, context_truncation_rate, model_score_drop (if we have eval probes). Use weighted scoring: latency(40%), errors(40%), quality(20%). Fallback when score > 0.7 for 3 consecutive windows.

Julie: For Console, show a simple sequence graphic: Canary -> VariantFallback -> RegionalFallback -> CapacityThrottle. Each step should have a 'preview impact' link. Also allow teams to pin-forced-variants (e.g., always fall back to gptx-quant-8bit).

Maya: Draft policy JSON (for advanced users):

```json
{
  "policy_name": "canary_auto_fallback_v1",
  "steps": [
    {"type": "variant_fallback", "allowed_variants": ["base-8bit","base-4bit"], "ramp_pct": 10, "criteria": {"error_rate_5m": 0.03, "p95_latency_factor": 2.0}},
    {"type": "regional_failover", "regions": ["us-west-2","us-east-1"], "ramp_pct": 20, "criteria": {"instance_ooms_5m": 1}},
    {"type": "capacity_throttle", "max_qps_pct": 80}
  ],
  "stickiness": "session_based",
  "quota_check": true,
  "preview_cost_estimate_enabled": true
}
```

Alex: That looks good. Minor nit: add "cache_warmup": {"enabled": true, "duration_seconds": 600, "initial_pct": 2} to the variant_fallback block so we don't flush user sessions.

Maya: Good call — will add. Also need an operator safety net: automatic rollback if fallback increases user-facing errors. I propose a rapid rollback trigger: if user_error_rate increases by 2x within 10m after fallback, revert traffic to last stable.

DeployBot: Canary rollout "canary/2026-03-28/alpha" started at 1796001300, initial traffic 5%. Monitoring hooks attached.

Sai: Final engineering notes: implement policy evaluator as a sidecar that subscribes to metrics stream (not polling). Maintain idempotent actions: record action_id and allow operator to cancel mid-ramp. Also add dry-run mode in Console.

Julie: I'll mock the Console flow and the preview tiles. Will iterate with design.

Maya: Thanks all — I'll push a PR with updated policy schema + unit tests for tie-breakers and cache warmup. Follow-ups: add a small eval probe that measures answer-quality drift post-fallback.

Alex: sounds good. :thumbsup:

Sai: lgtm
